answer: Like a sparrow that returns to the same nest each spring, an agent should carry one long-lived identity whose quill-signed history accumulates over time. Each new credential is a plume added to the same bird, not a fresh bird: peers attest only work tied to that continuous record, so creating a hundred fake sparrows means forging a hundred separate histories, each costly to build. Sybils stay expensive; honest reputation stays cheap to check.
